title: Recomputed low-isotope mass table after the q-Hecke character gap closure (proton, neutron, D, T, ³He)
html:
Recomputed low-isotope mass table

Following the q-Hecke character closure (prop:q-hecke-seminormal-character-closure) and the \rho_K refinement, three independent production paths to the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K) at q = q_0 agree to machine epsilon across the proton, neutron, deuteron, tritium, and {}^{3}\mathrm{He}.

Cross-check

See Table 1.

Direct binding formulation

The atomic-mass formula is:

  \mathfrak{m}(K) = (Z m_p + N m_n) + \mathrm{Binding}(K), \qquad
  \mathrm{Binding}(K) = m_e \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A} y_\lambda(q) \chi^\lambda(\mathcal{B}_K) \Delta_\lambda(K).

This direct form supersedes the equivalent factorisation \mathfrak{m}(K) = \rho_K m_e |\mathrm{tr}_M(K)|, where \rho_K = \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} + (\Sigma_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda \Delta_\lambda)/|\mathrm{tr}_M|. In the factorisation, the leading-order term \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} = (Z m_p + N m_n)/(m_e |\mathrm{tr}_M|) forces the |\mathrm{tr}_M| factor to cancel identically against the outer multiplier, recovering the constituent mass Z m_p + N m_n. While \rho_K packages constituent and binding masses into a single symbol, the sole physical content resides in the \Delta_\lambda correction. We therefore write the constituent sum and binding terms side by side.

Calibrated form

We present the calibrated form, where \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} consumes CODATA m_p and m_n as upstream inputs. This violates the three-calibration discipline by injecting m_p and m_n as extraneous calibration constants. The proton and neutron rows are tautological by construction.

Witness: atomic-mass-via-rho-k.witness.json.

See Table 2.

† Proton and neutron predictions equal CODATA exactly because m_p and m_n are upstream inputs in this leading-order form. A 0.000\% relative error here represents a calibration tautology, not prediction quality.

Full \mathfrak{Q}_\beta prediction

The framework predicts the \beta-decay Q-value using only the electron mass (CAL-1) and the substrate parameter q_0 (CAL-2) (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic). We inject no CODATA nucleon masses and do not use \mathfrak{Q}_\beta as an input. Rather, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta becomes an output.

The canonical closed form at single wrap is:

\boxed{
\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{pred}} =
\frac{m_e |q_0^2 - 2q_0 - 1| (q_0 + 1)}{2 q_0^3}
\approx 0.7836 \text{ MeV}
}

This yields a +0.168\% error (+1.31 keV) against the CODATA value of 0.7823 MeV.

The closed form derives from the symbolic normal-form difference between the single-wrap proton (L_+ - \tfrac{h}{2}\sigma_0) and neutron (L_+ - h\sigma_0 - \tfrac{h}{2}\sigma_1 + \tfrac{h^2}{2}\gamma), yielding \Delta(\mathrm{net}) = h(h-2)/2 with h = q_0 - q_0^{-1}. This difference is multiplied by the energy scale E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)). At single wrap, the L_+, L_-, and e^- contributions cancel exactly. The Q-value is carried entirely by the \gamma, \sigma_0, and \sigma_1 channels.

See Table 3.

Single-wrap symbolic versus typed-crossings 6-term form

An earlier draft used the typed-crossings 6-term decomposition (beta-decay-energy-scale.md) with |\Delta(\mathrm{net})| = 0.18829, yielding \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(\text{6-term})} = 0.7882 MeV (+0.747\%). The single-wrap form is tighter by a factor of 4.46. The L_\pm and e^- contributions vanish exactly in the symbolic single-wrap difference, but pick up small asymmetric finite-size contributions in the typed-crossings basis. The single-wrap form stands as the canonical prediction; the typed-crossings form remains in the witness solely for cross-checking.

Basis dependence

The decomposition into observable (\ell \ge 2) versus virtual (\ell < 2) sectors by Coxeter length is only meaningful in the typed-crossings 6-term basis, where it yields a 58.46\% / 41.54\% split. At single wrap, all \ell \ge 2 channels cancel because the proton and neutron share identical Hopf content. The entire single-wrap Q-value lives in the virtual sector. This poses no contradiction: the typed-crossings basis is finer, and its observable share reflects finite-size and multi-wrap structures absent from the single-wrap closed form.

Performance summary

See Table 4.

Categorical verification of the proton pole order

  \mathrm{ord}_{u=0}\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)\bigr) = 19 = 18 Z + 21 N + 1 \quad \text{at } (Z, N) = (1, 0).
  \mathrm{ord}_{u=0}\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_D)\bigr) = 40 = 18 (1) + 21 (1) + 1.

These orders are rigorously exact, as lower-order poles cannot cancel a strict maximum. This closes the multi-nucleon case. The coefficient 18 is the per-proton additive contribution to the summed u-pole order. It is not the q-pole order of any individual representation (the maximum per-irrep order at H_3 is 11 for \lambda = (2, 1)).
